messages:
Priya S: We're blocked on the 'atomic-apply' API for multi-route flag rollouts. Console needs a server-side primitive so UI can do Preview -> Staged -> Commit without races. Thoughts?
Marco B: what are the failure modes we care about? partial apply across routes, double-apply, and quota oversubscription when we shift traffic.
Diego L: +1. My vote is a 2PC-esque flow but simpler: 1) POST /config/apply-intent -> returns apply_id + preview diff, 2) POST /config/apply-stage with {apply_id, weight_map} to assign percent per cohort, 3) POST /config/apply-commit?apply_id=... to activate. Each step idempotent via an idempotency_key.
Tara J: prefer fewer round trips. Could we fold preview+intent into one call: POST /config/preview?dry_run=true returns apply_id. Then activation is a single call with an if-match style header (ETag) to do optimistic concurrency.
Priya S: console team likes three steps because we show a live preview and let PMs adjust weights. But backend must guarantee no partial activation if commit fails mid-way. How do we handle node-level apply failures?
Diego L: backend will maintain apply_state in config-store: PENDING -> STAGED -> COMMITTING -> ACTIVE. During COMMITTING we coordinate via per-cluster apply workers that ack. If >X% clusters fail ack within timeout, rollback to STAGED. We'll emit events for visibility.
Marco B: timeout? who decides? Ops wants default 60s but per-apply override. Also we need a manual abort endpoint.
Tara J: also need to consider quotas. If a rollout increases route cost, quota pools could starve other features. Can we add a safety_headroom_pct parameter to apply_intent that simulator uses to estimate headroom and fail fast?
Priya S: yes. Proposal: apply-intent takes {safety_headroom_pct: 20} default. The projection sim runs against recent 1h usage and rejects if projected consumption > (quota - safety_headroom).
Diego L: projection algorithm: simulate cohort weight distribution using tenant-hash, scale past usage by weight delta, include cached inference of per-tenant QPS. We'll expose endpoint POST /config/simulate with same payload for console preview.
Marco B: sounds compute-heavy. Keep simulate async with job_id and optional realtime stream via kafka topic config.simulate.<job_id>.console. Console subscribes if available.
Tara J: UX note: console must surface estimated 95th pct of per-tenant QPS post-rollout and a small "confidence" text when simulation is sampled. Also show recommended safety_headroom based on quota fragility.
Priya S: good. Telemetry: ingest should receive config.apply.intent and config.apply.outcome events. Include fields: apply_id, flag_keys, weight_map, safety_headroom_pct, sample_rate, sim_job_id, result{status,reason}.
Diego L: adding to that: emit per-route pre/post aggregates so alerting rules can compare p50/p95 latency and error_rate. We'll tag with apply_id to link metrics.
Marco B: alerting rules proposal: auto-rollback if either (1) p50_latency + delta_ms > 200ms for 5m OR (2) error_rate increases by >1.5 percentage points AND failure is correlated across >10% of tenants. Implement correlation by tenant-bucketed histograms.
Tara J: correlation is important; single noisy tenant shouldn't yank the rollout. Also console should show a heatmap of effected tenants (anonymized buckets) with a link to open an ops ticket.
Priya S: ops integration: apply-intent should optionally set notify_ops: true which creates a runbook stub with apply_id and links. Good for larger rollouts.
Diego L: API details: use If-Match: "etag" on commit call for optimistic concurrency. For idempotency, accept Idempotency-Key header. Return 409 with current_state and reason on conflict.
Marco B: how about rollback semantics? If commit fails we transition to FAILED and either auto-revert to previous ACTIVE state or leave STAGED depending on auto_rollback flag in intent.
Tara J: default auto_rollback=true for safety. Allow auto_rollback=false for emergency ops who will manually debug. Need audit trail showing who triggered apply, at what time, and all intermediate states.
Priya S: logging/telemetry: store an immutable apply ledger entry per state change in clickhouse for 90d. Also push streaming events to kafka topic config.apply.events for console and alerts.
Diego L: implementation note: config-store needs a lightweight transactional write (we can use optimistic CAS against current_version). Avoid long synchronous locks across clusters. Workers pull apply changes and attempt local activation idempotently.
Marco B: migration: existing console calls /flags/update will be supported by a compatibility adapter that translates to apply-intent + commit for simple single-route toggles. We'll run adapter for 7 days and then flip clients.
Tara J: security: restrict apply endpoints to service-role tokens and require MFA for apply sizes > 25% traffic or > N tenants. Console should show a confirmation modal for large apply.
Priya S: final decisions summary: POST /config/apply-intent returns apply_id + preview; POST /config/simulate is async job; POST /config/apply-stage sets weights; POST /config/apply-commit?apply_id=... does commit with If-Match; default auto_rollback=true; safety_headroom_pct default 20; idempotency and etag support; telemetry events pushed to kafka.
ingest-bot: Deploy scheduled: config-service v3 -> canary at 2026-03-25T04:00:00Z.
Diego L: I'll sketch an RFC with sample payloads and state diagram. Priya/Tara can we pair on console mockups for staged UI and the confirmation flows?
Priya S: yes, let's pair tomorrow 10:30. Tara will draft help copy about safety_headroom and why quota simulation matters.
Tara J: will do. Also adding a small blurb in release notes about the 7-day adapter compatibility window. :memo:
